site_description: The community guide to MeshCore in Europe: getting started, hardware, local groups, coverage maps and repeaters. Non-commercial and open source.
hero_title: Off the grid, on the mesh.
hero_lead: MeshCore sends messages by radio, without the internet or a subscription. Europe's meshes connect into one. Here, their communities share what they learn.
paths_title: Where do you want to start?
path_new_desc: What a mesh is, and what MeshCore can and cannot do.
path_offgrid_desc: Pick a board for hiking, sailing, events or a power cut.
path_build_desc: Radio, antennas, tools and projects from other communities.
path_grow_desc: Plan and place a repeater that covers your area.
path_local_desc: Find your local group, its chats and its channels.
why_costs_desc: Buy a radio once. Messages cost nothing: no SIM card, data plan or subscription.
why_infra_desc: Keeps working when mobile networks and the internet are down or out of reach. Messages go from radio to radio, over the air.
why_open_desc: The firmware and its protocol are open source, so anyone can build on them. Open apps, tools and libraries already do.
why_privacy_desc: Direct messages are encrypted end to end. You need no account or phone number to join.
why_routing_desc: Your first message floods through the repeaters, the nodes on roofs and masts that pass messages on. A message that floods can carry a region, and repeaters only pass on the regions they serve, so it stays in its area.
why_community_desc: Local groups across Europe put up repeaters, share settings and help newcomers. Find the one near you under Local groups.

presets_source: From the MeshCore project's preset list, checked
gain_label: The beam of a dipole and a fibreglass collinear, cut through the mast and seen from the side, to scale. The collinear reaches a node far along the horizon. Only the dipole reaches a node steep below.
rz_forged_label: A packet goes from the sender through 3 repeaters to you. The sender starts its path with 3 made-up IDs. Each repeater adds its own ID at the end, so the end of the path is real and the start is not.
rz_gate_label: Regions round a repeater as rings: messages without a region outside, then a country, a province and the repeater's own region in the middle. When the repeater transmits more than 35% of the last minute, the outer rings stop one by one. Its own region keeps passing.
rz_gate_step_calm: Under 35%: your repeater passes on every region it holds.
rz_gate_step_none: Over 35%: messages without a region stop.
rz_gate_step_wide: Still busy: the widest region stops too. Your own region always passes.
rz_copies_label: One packet from a sender nobody sees passes 4 repeaters. 3 observers each report the copy they heard, with its path. The copy with the shortest path, 1 repeater, was heard closest to the sender.
rz_copies_observer: Observer, with the path of its copy
rz_copies_shortest: Shortest path: closest to the sender
device.heltec-wifi-lora-32-v3.notes: A bare board: add a case, an antenna and a battery. The ESP32 uses too much power for a small solar repeater.
device.heltec-wifi-lora-32-v4.notes: The high-power version transmits up to 28 dBm, above the European limit with most antennas: the repeater guide shows how to stay within it. The basic version costs under 25 euros, the high-power version more. The R8 version has more memory and needs its own firmware build.
device.heltec-mesh-node-t114.notes: Low-power nRF52 board and a common base for solar repeaters. Screen and GPS are optional when you order; with them it costs more than 25 euros.
device.heltec-wireless-tracker.notes: Board with built-in GPS. Bring your own battery and case.
device.heltec-wireless-paper.notes: The e-paper screen stays readable in sunlight. No battery included.
device.lilygo-t-echo.notes: Pocket handheld with an e-paper screen and GPS. A version with a bigger battery exists too.
device.lilygo-t-deck-plus.notes: Physical keyboard, trackball and touch screen. The Plus adds GPS and a 2000 mAh battery.
device.lilygo-t-beam-supreme.notes: Holds an 18650 cell, not included. Pick the SX1262 version: the LR1121 version has no official build.
device.rak-wisblock-rak4631.notes: Modular: clip-on modules add GPS, a screen or sensors. The base board has a solar input.
device.rak-wismesh-tag.notes: Slim weatherproof badge with built-in antennas.
device.seeed-sensecap-t1000-e.notes: Credit-card size, dust- and splash-proof (IP65), no screen. Uses the LR1110 radio instead of the more common SX1262.
device.seeed-xiao-nrf52840-wio-sx1262.no: A tiny two-board stack. Solder on a battery for portable use.
device.seeed-wio-tracker-l1-pro.notes: Comes in a case with screen, GPS and battery. Lite and e-ink versions exist too.
device.seeed-sensecap-solar-node-p1.note: Weatherproof case with a 5 W solar panel, four 18650 cells and GPS, made for repeaters.
device.heltec-wifi-lora-32-v4-expansion-: A V4 board in a metal case with a touch screen. GPS and an 18650 cell are options when you order. MeshCore shows the screen but does not use touch yet.
device.heltec-wireless-stick-lite-v3.not: The V3 without a screen. A bare board: add a case, an antenna and a battery.
device.heltec-wireless-tracker-v2.notes: Board with GPS and a solar connector. It transmits up to 28 dBm, above the European limit with most antennas: the repeater guide shows how to stay within it.
device.heltec-vision-master-e213.notes: Board with an e-paper screen that stays readable in sunlight. Bring your own battery and case.
device.heltec-vision-master-e290.notes: Like the E213 with a bigger e-paper screen. Bring your own battery and case.
device.heltec-vision-master-t190.notes: Board with a colour screen. Bring your own battery and case.
device.heltec-mesh-node-t1.notes: Card-sized tag with GPS and a small screen, dust- and splash-proof (IP65).
device.heltec-meshpocket.notes: A power bank with a node inside, and a magnetic wireless charger for your phone. Also sold with 10000 mAh.
device.heltec-meshsolar.notes: Board for a solar repeater: takes one to four cells and an 18 to 24 V panel. GPS and a screen are add-ons.
device.heltec-meshtower-v2.notes: Weatherproof metal case with three cells and a 10 W solar panel, made for repeaters. GPS is optional. The 30 dBm version is above the European limit: the repeater guide shows how to stay within it.
device.lilygo-t-echo-lite.notes: Smaller T-Echo with a GPS add-on module. Sold with or without a case.
device.lilygo-t-echo-card.notes: Credit-card size with GPS, a speaker and a small solar panel that only tops up the battery.
device.lilygo-t-impulse-plus.notes: Wristband with GPS, a tiny screen and a vibration motor.
device.lilygo-t-deck.notes: Keyboard and trackball like the T-Deck Plus, without GPS or battery. Pick a version with LoRa: one without exists.
device.lilygo-t-beam.notes: The classic T-Beam with the older SX1276 radio. Holds an 18650 cell, not included.
device.lilygo-t-beam-1w.notes: Transmits up to 32 dBm, far above the European limit: the repeater guide shows how to stay within it. Needs a 7.4 V battery, which it does not charge.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m1.notes: Handheld with an e-paper screen and GPS.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m2.notes: Small handheld with an OLED screen. Also sold without a battery.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m3.notes: Dust- and waterproof (IP66) tracker with GPS, no screen.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m4.notes: A power bank with a node and GPS inside, no screen.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m5.notes: Like the M1 with an ESP32 processor: more features, shorter battery life.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m6.notes: Weatherproof case (IP65) with a 6 W solar panel, two 18650 cells and GPS, made for repeaters.
device.elecrow-thinknode-m7.notes: Indoor box with an Ethernet port, powered over USB or the network cable (PoE).
device.elecrow-thinknode-m9.notes: Works on its own with a full keyboard, colour screen and GPS. It ships with Ripple firmware; standard MeshCore runs on it too.
device.seeed-wio-tracker-l1.notes: The L1 Pro without case and battery. Has GPS and a solar connector.
device.seeed-wio-tracker-l1-eink.notes: The L1 with an e-paper screen, without case and battery. MeshCore runs on it as companion only.
device.seeed-sensecap-solar-node-p1-basi: The P1-Pro without cells and GPS: add four 18650 cells yourself. The holder only takes button-top cells. Common flat-top cells fit with a small magnet on each.
device.seeed-sensecap-meshtracker-x1.not: Card-sized and dust- and waterproof (IP66), no screen. Charges over USB-C and vibrates on a new message.
device.seeed-xiao-esp32s3-wio-sx1262.not: The XIAO kit with an ESP32 instead of the nRF52: Wi-Fi, but more power use.
device.rak-wismesh-1w-booster.notes: Transmits up to 30 dBm, above the European limit: the repeater guide shows how to stay within it. Each version runs either on a battery or on 5 V, check the label.
device.bq-station-g3.notes: Modular base station with an amplifier up to 35 dBm, far above the European limit: set the jumpers and transmit power for your country. Needs a 9 to 19 V supply.
device.bq-nano-g2-ultra.notes: Rugged handheld with a built-in antenna designed to work close to your body. The battery is optional.
device.m5stack-unit-c6l.notes: Small module in a plastic shell, powered over USB-C. No battery input.
device.meshnology-w12.notes: Open-source board with battery and solar inputs. It transmits up to 30 dBm, above the European limit: the repeater guide shows how to stay within it.

map.de-meshcore-de-regions.desc: Editable map of MeshCore regions and local groups, mostly in Germany.

project.meshcore-py.desc: Python bindings for controlling a MeshCore companion radio over serial, Bluetooth or TCP.
project.meshcore-cli.desc: Command-line client for sending messages to and managing MeshCore nodes from a terminal.

project.meshcore-map.desc: Source of the official node map where owners can publish their nodes.

project.litescope.desc: Lightweight self-hosted dashboard for watching a MeshCore network. The Estonian community runs one.

project.potato-mesh.desc: Federated community dashboard for MeshCore and other mesh networks, used by Berlin Chaos Mesh.

project.lora-harvester-box.desc: Open hardware board pairing an STM32WL LoRa chip with an energy harvester, for very low-power LoRa nodes, MeshCore among them.

project.dmc-triangulator.desc: Narrows down where a node is from the repeaters that heard it, as a first search area before a local hunt.
project.kiekr.desc: Phone app for messaging on the mesh that also maps coverage and can upload what it hears to analysers.
project.meshmapper.desc: Coverage map built from wardriving, with regional instances, its own MQTT broker and an open API.
project.trail-mate.desc: Offline handheld firmware for the LilyGO T-LoRa Pager and T-Deck, with GPS navigation and team messaging over MeshCore and Meshtastic.
project.remote-terminal.desc: Self-hosted client for a MeshCore radio that keeps and decrypts captured packets on a server, with bots and MQTT.
project.meshpoint.desc: Raspberry Pi base station with an SX1302 or SX1303 concentrator that listens on several channels at once, with a local dashboard.
project.easyskymesh.desc: Firmware fork that saves power for repeaters and sensor nodes running on a battery or a small solar panel.

project.wio-tracker-l1-pro.desc: Companion firmware for the Seeed Wio Tracker L1 Pro with a user interface on the device itself.
project.meshcore-one.desc: Native MeshCore app for iPhone, iPad and Mac.

project.meshcore-packet-capture.desc: Python script that captures packets from a companion radio and publishes them to MQTT.
project.cardputer-adv-sosprz.desc: Companion firmware for the M5Stack Cardputer ADV with the Cap LoRa868, flashed with M5Burner.
project.lora-wideband-decoder.desc: Software-defined radio receiver that decodes MeshCore, Meshtastic and LoRaWAN traffic across a wide band, with a local web page.
project.mc-webui.desc: Web interface on top of meshcore-cli, to message from a browser.
project.meshfirmware.desc: Scripts for Linux and Windows that pick, build and flash MeshCore and Meshtastic firmware over USB.
project.repeater-mqtt-gateway.desc: Repeater firmware that also connects the mesh to an MQTT broker, in both directions.
project.tak-meshcore.desc: Plugin that lets the ATAK situational awareness app use a MeshCore companion radio over Bluetooth.
project.meshcore-decoder.desc: TypeScript library that decodes MeshCore packets, decryption included.
project.mesh-loader.desc: Dual boot for the Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3 and V4: keep two firmwares on one board and switch between them.
project.meshcore-proxy.desc: TCP proxy that makes a companion radio on USB or Bluetooth reachable for apps on other computers.
project.roadstr.desc: Road event reporting without a central server: signed Nostr events, carried over MeshCore when there is no internet.
project.domca-docs.desc: Documentation in Dutch and English, from your first node to how the protocol, the firmware and the radio work. It is written with help from AI tools, so check firmware details against the MeshCore source.
guides_card_get_started_desc: From a new board to your first message on the mesh, in 6 steps.
guides_card_devices_desc: Compare boards by role, price and power source, and pick the one that fits.
guides_card_settings_desc: The radio preset your area uses, and the settings your neighbours changed.
guides_card_antenna_desc: A tuned antenna and a short cable win more range than extra power. Check the antenna on your companion, and choose, connect and mount one for a repeater.
guides_card_repeater_desc: A repeater passes messages on for everyone around it. Placement, the commands to set it up, and the legal limits on 868 MHz.
guides_card_resilient_desc: Something disrupts the mesh near you? Find out what it is, and switch on the setting on your repeater that stops it.
guides_card_filter_desc: Keep your repeater from passing on junk, such as a bot that never stops or a noisy channel.
guides_card_mqtt_desc: An observer is a node that forwards what it hears over MQTT. Set one up for a map or an analyser.
guides_card_mctomqtt_desc: Send what your repeater hears to any MQTT broker: your own, or the Analyzer.
guides_card_cli_desc: The commands of a repeater, each with what it does.
firmware_card_flasher_desc: Put MeshCore on your board from your browser, over USB.
firmware_card_console_desc: Type commands to your repeater from your browser, over USB.
firmware_card_changelog_desc: See what changed in each MeshCore release, and whether your node needs it.
area_device_companion: In the app on your companion
area_change_nl_regions: Add the regions your repeater serves, each inside the one above it: Europe, Benelux, the Netherlands, your province and your city. Your province becomes the default.
area_change_strict_regions: Drop packets without a region, so they do not travel across Europe. Add the regions first.
area_change_zero_hop: Send the advert your direct neighbours hear every 4 hours.
area_change_path_hash: Use a 2-byte path hash: it tells 65,536 repeaters apart instead of 256.
area_change_loop: Drop flood packets that loop back through your repeater. A repeater set up with 1.18 or later already does this.
area_change_nl_companion_region: In the app's experimental settings, set the default region to nl. Give each channel its region, such as nl-nh for North Holland.
area_change_companion_path_hash: In the app's experimental settings, set the default path hash size to 2 bytes.
area_source_preset: Preset from the MeshCore project's list
area_add_body: Does your local group use its own preset, or change settings? Send them in, with a link to where you decided them.
regions_title: Regions: from Europe to your town
regions_body: A region is a code for an area. Regions sit inside each other: Europe, your country, your province, and in some places your town. Give your repeater the regions it sits in, each inside the one above it. It passes on messages for any of them.
regions_map_body: Which codes are in use differs per area. The map shows the regions the repeaters around you use: use the ones your neighbours use, or your repeater drops their messages.
regions_region: Your region, if your area uses one
regions_town: Your town, if your area uses one
regions_cmd_hint: Pick your province, or type its code over the highlighted value, then copy.
area_ph_hint: Type your own values over the highlighted ones, then copy.
area_map_label: Map of the areas and their radio preset
area_others_title: The rest of the EU and the UK
area_country_missing: Your country is not in the list? Ask your local group which preset it uses, or {link}.
area_country_eu: {country} has no preset of its own in the MeshCore app. It uses {preset}, the preset MeshCore names for the EU and the UK.
area_others_body: These countries have no preset of their own in the MeshCore app. They use EU/UK (Narrow), the preset MeshCore names for them.
cmd_reboot_desc: Restarts the node straight away, and the node sends you no reply. Use it to apply settings that only take effect after a reboot.
cmd_poweroff_desc: Switches the node off on boards that support it, without sending a reply. You need the power button or a power cycle to start it again.
cmd_clkreboot_desc: Sets the clock back to an early date and restarts the node without a reply. Use it when the clock runs ahead and refuses to go back.
cmd_clock_desc: Shows the node's clock in UTC, or sets it to a Unix time in seconds. The clock only moves forward, so use clkreboot first to go back.
cmd_clock_sync_desc: Sets the node's clock to the time your companion sends with this command. It only works over the mesh, because the serial console sends no time.
cmd_start_ota_desc: Starts a firmware update over the air on ESP32 and nRF52 boards that support it. ESP32 opens a WiFi access point, nRF52 starts a Bluetooth update.
cmd_erase_desc: Wipes the file system of the node, including its settings and identity, from serial only. Use it for a factory reset, because you cannot undo it.
cmd_room_post_desc: Posts a message in the room as the room server itself. Everyone in the room receives it like any other post.
cmd_advert_desc: Sends a flood advert now, so nodes across the mesh learn about this node. Use it after you change the name or the location.
cmd_advert_zerohop_desc: Sends an advert to direct neighbours only, and no repeater passes it on. Use it to announce the node nearby without loading the whole mesh.
cmd_advert_interval_desc: Sets how often, in minutes, the node sends a zero-hop advert to its neighbours. Use 0 to stop them; any saved change also stops intervals under 60.
cmd_flood_advert_interval_desc: Sets how often, in hours, the node sends a flood advert across the whole mesh. Use 0 to stop the automatic flood adverts from this node completely.
cmd_neighbours_desc: Lists the repeaters this node heard directly, with the most recent one first. Each line shows a key prefix, seconds since heard and the SNR times 4.
cmd_neighbour_remove_desc: Removes every neighbour whose public key starts with the hex prefix you give. Use it to clear an old repeater from the neighbour list.
cmd_discover_neighbours_desc: Asks the repeaters in direct range to reply, and adds each reply to the neighbours. Use it to fill the list without waiting for their adverts. A repeater with both advert intervals at 0, or with repeat off, stays silent.
cmd_clear_stats_desc: Resets the packet, radio and core counters of the node back to zero. Use it before you measure the traffic over a set period.
cmd_stats_core_desc: Shows the battery voltage, uptime, error count and transmit queue length of the node. It works on the serial console only, not over the mesh.
cmd_stats_radio_desc: Shows the noise floor, the last RSSI and SNR, and the airtime spent sending and receiving. It works on the serial console only, not over the mesh.
cmd_stats_packets_desc: Shows how many packets the node received and sent, split into flood and direct. It works on the serial console only, not over the mesh.
cmd_log_capture_desc: Starts or stops writing every packet the node receives and sends to a log file. Use it to capture traffic, then read it with the log command.
cmd_log_erase_desc: Deletes the packet log file from the storage of the node. Use it to free space or to start a clean capture.
cmd_log_desc: Prints the captured packet log, line by line, to the serial console. It works on the serial console only, not over the mesh.
cmd_ver_desc: Shows the firmware version and the build date of the node. Use it to check which release runs before you update.
cmd_board_desc: Shows the name of the hardware board that the firmware was built for. Use it to check that you flashed the right firmware.
cmd_power_desc: Shows the battery voltage, and whether USB, solar, external power and the charger are active. A board that cannot detect USB or solar shows n/a for it.
cmd_public_key_desc: Shows the full public key of the node in hex. Share it when someone asks which node is yours, or when a repeater owner gives your companion a role with setperm.
cmd_role_desc: Shows which firmware the node runs: repeater, room_server or sensor. Use it to check the role before you change settings remotely.
cmd_bootloader_ver_desc: Shows the version of the bootloader that runs on nRF52 boards. On every other board the node replies that the command is unsupported.
cmd_pwrmgt_support_desc: Shows whether this firmware build includes power management for nRF52 boards. The other pwrmgt commands need this support to give an answer.
cmd_pwrmgt_source_desc: Shows whether the node runs on external power or on its battery. Only firmware builds with nRF52 power management support give you this answer.
cmd_pwrmgt_bootreason_desc: Shows why the node last reset and why it last shut down. Use it to find out why a node restarted on its own.
cmd_pwrmgt_bootmv_desc: Shows the battery voltage in millivolts that the node measured at boot. Only firmware builds with nRF52 power management support give you this answer.
cmd_radio_desc: Sets the frequency, bandwidth, spreading factor and coding rate the node uses. Every node in your mesh needs the same values; reboot to apply them.
cmd_tx_desc: Sets the transmit power of the LoRa chip in dBm, and it applies straight away. Boards with an extra amplifier send out more than this value.
cmd_tempradio_desc: Switches to other radio settings for a set number of minutes, without saving them. Use it to test new settings remotely, with an automatic way back.
cmd_freq_desc: Sets only the frequency in MHz, and the set form works on serial only. Reboot the node afterwards, because the new frequency applies only after a restart.
cmd_radio_rxgain_desc: Turns the boosted receive gain of the radio chip on or off. A radio without this mode replies that the setting is unsupported on it.
cmd_radio_fem_rxgain_desc: Turns the receive amplifier of an external radio front end on or off. Only boards with a front end you can control support it.
cmd_radio_fem_txgain_desc: Switches the transmit gain of an external radio front end between its 2 levels. Only boards with a front end you can control support it.
cmd_extra_sf_desc: Makes an LR2021 radio also listen for up to 3 extra spreading factors. Give them as a comma list; other radios do not accept the set form.
cmd_repeat_desc: Turns forwarding of packets from other nodes on or off. Switch it off to keep a node on the air without repeating. A room server refuses to switch it on.
cmd_path_hash_mode_desc: Sets the hash size this node writes into the paths of packets it sends. Mode 0 uses 1 byte, 1 uses 2 and 2 uses 3.
cmd_loop_detect_desc: Drops flood packets that already carry this repeater's hash in their path too often. A stricter level drops a looping packet after fewer repeats. A repeater updated from an older version keeps the level it had.
cmd_txdelay_desc: Sets the random wait before the node repeats a flood packet, scaled by airtime. A higher value avoids collisions between repeaters but adds delay.
cmd_direct_txdelay_desc: Sets the random wait before the node repeats a direct packet, scaled by airtime. Direct packets need less wait, because fewer nodes repeat them.
cmd_rxdelay_desc: Holds weak flood packets back before processing, so paths with a strong signal repeat first. Use 0 to process every packet straight away, whatever its signal.
cmd_dutycycle_desc: Limits the share of time the node spends transmitting, as a percentage. Set it to the limit that applies to your frequency band.
cmd_af_desc: Sets the airtime factor, the older way to limit the duty cycle of the node. Use dutycycle instead; an af of 9 equals 10 percent.
cmd_int_thresh_desc: Treats the channel as busy when it reads this many dB above the noise floor. The node then waits before it transmits; 0 switches the check off.
cmd_cad_desc: Makes the radio listen for activity on the channel before each transmission. The node waits with sending while the channel is busy.
cmd_agc_reset_interval_desc: Resets the automatic gain control of the radio every set number of seconds. The node rounds down to a multiple of 4; 0 switches it off.
cmd_multi_acks_desc: Sends extra copies of each acknowledgement to improve delivery on weak links. Use 0 to send every acknowledgement only once, without extra copies.
cmd_flood_max_desc: Sets the number of hops after which this node stops repeating a flood packet. Lower it to keep floods from travelling far across the mesh.
cmd_flood_max_unscoped_desc: Sets the hop limit for flood packets without a region. Lower it to keep that traffic close to home.
cmd_flood_max_advert_desc: Sets the hop limit for the flood adverts this node repeats. Lower it to keep adverts from crossing the whole mesh.
cmd_name_desc: Sets the name that other nodes see in the adverts of this node. The characters [ ] \ : , ? * are not allowed.
cmd_lat_desc: Sets the latitude in decimal degrees that this node shares in its adverts. Use it with lon to put the node in the right place on a map.
cmd_lon_desc: Sets the longitude in decimal degrees that this node shares in its adverts. Use it with lat to put the node in the right place on a map.
cmd_prv_key_desc: Shows or replaces the private key, which defines the identity of the node. The get form works on serial only; reboot after you set a key.
cmd_password_desc: Changes the admin password and echoes the new one back so you can check it. Change it on every new node, because the default is public.
cmd_guest_password_desc: Sets the guest password; on a room server it gives read and write access. Share it with the people you want to let into the room.
cmd_owner_info_desc: Sets contact text that others can request from the node, such as your name. Type a | character wherever you want a new line to start.
cmd_adc_multiplier_desc: Corrects the battery voltage reading of the node with a multiplier for your board. Use 0 to go back to the value the board itself defines.
cmd_powersaving_desc: Lets the node sleep between radio activity to save battery power. It works on nRF52 boards and on ESP32 builds without a bridge.
cmd_setperm_desc: Gives a companion a role on this node, found by its public key. Use 0 to remove the entry; the other roles need the full key.
cmd_acl_desc: Prints the access list with the permissions and public key of each companion. It works on the serial console only, not over the mesh.
cmd_allow_read_only_desc: Lets people with a wrong or empty password join a room server with read-only access. Switch it off to admit only people who know the password.
cmd_region_desc: Shows the full region tree of the node, with the flood flag of each region. An F means flooding is allowed and ^ marks the home region.
cmd_region_load_desc: Starts bulk input of a region tree, one region per line, indented with spaces. Add F to allow flooding, and send a blank line to finish.
cmd_region_save_desc: Saves your region changes to the storage of the node, so they survive a reboot. Run it after every region change that you want to keep.
cmd_region_flood_desc: Allows or blocks repeating of flood packets for a region. Use * for the packets that carry no region at all.
cmd_region_get_desc: Shows one region with its parent, and an F when flooding is allowed for it. Use it to check a single region without reading the whole tree.
cmd_region_home_desc: Shows or sets the home region, which the region tree marks with a ^. Run region save afterwards to keep the change after a reboot.
cmd_region_default_desc: Shows or sets the region the node puts on its own flood packets, like adverts. The node saves the change at once; <null> clears it.
cmd_region_put_desc: Adds a region under the wildcard or under a parent you name, with flooding allowed. Run region save afterwards to keep the new region after a reboot.
cmd_region_def_desc: Builds a region tree on one line, each name a child of the one before. Write name|jump to continue the next name from an earlier region.
cmd_region_remove_desc: Removes a region by its exact name, once it has no child regions left. Run region save afterwards to make the removal survive a reboot.
cmd_region_list_desc: Lists the names of the regions where flooding is allowed, or where it is blocked. Use it for a quick check without the full tree.
cmd_gps_desc: Shows whether the GPS is on, has a fix and how many satellites it sees. The on and off forms switch the GPS and save the choice.
cmd_gps_diag_desc: Shows whether the GPS is switched on, how many satellites it sees and whether it has a fix. Use it when the node gets no position.
cmd_gps_sync_desc: Sets the clock of the node from the time the GPS receives. Use it when the node has no other source of correct time.
cmd_gps_setloc_desc: Copies the current GPS position into the saved latitude and longitude of the node. Use it once at the site, then switch the GPS off.
cmd_gps_advert_desc: Chooses the position in adverts: none, live GPS or the saved lat and lon. Use none to keep the location of the node private.
cmd_sensor_list_desc: Lists the custom settings of the sensor manager with their values. A long list ends with the index you continue from.
cmd_sensor_setting_desc: Reads or changes one custom setting of the sensor manager by its name. Use sensor list first to see which names the board offers.
cmd_io_desc: Reads or writes the GPIO pins of the board as a hex bit mask. Put r, s or t before the mask to reset, set or toggle bits.
cmd_bridge_type_desc: Shows which bridge this firmware has built in: rs232, espnow or none. Use it to check that you flashed a bridge build.
cmd_bridge_enabled_desc: Turns the bridge on or off; it copies packets between the mesh and another link. That link is a serial cable or ESP-NOW, depending on the build.
cmd_bridge_delay_desc: Sets how many milliseconds the bridge waits before it passes a packet on. Raise it when bridged packets collide with traffic on the mesh.
cmd_bridge_source_desc: Chooses whether the bridge copies the packets this node receives or the ones it sends. Type rx or tx to set it; get replies with logRx or logTx.
cmd_bridge_baud_desc: Sets the serial speed of an RS-232 bridge in baud. Both ends of the serial cable need the same speed.
cmd_bridge_channel_desc: Sets the WiFi channel that an ESP-NOW bridge uses for its link. Every bridge that talks to this one needs the same channel.
cmd_bridge_secret_desc: Sets the shared secret that scrambles packets on an ESP-NOW bridge. Use the same secret on every bridge that talks to this one.
cmd_eth_status_desc: Shows the IP address and port of the Ethernet console, or that it is offline. It works on the serial and Ethernet consoles, not over the mesh.
cmd_pin_desc: Sets the Bluetooth PIN your phone asks for when it pairs, after a reboot. With 0, a board with a screen shows a new PIN each start, and one without uses 123456.
cmd_tz_offset_desc: Sets your time zone in whole hours from UTC. The companion uses it for the clock on its screen.
cmd_wifi_ssid_desc: Shows or sets the name of the WiFi network the companion joins. Set wifi.pwd too, then reboot to connect.
cmd_wifi_pwd_desc: Shows or sets the password of the WiFi network, and reboot to apply it. A contact you allow to send commands can read it too.
cmd_wifi_enabled_desc: Switches WiFi on with 1 or off with 0, after a reboot. Without a network name, the companion does not start WiFi.
cmd_wifi_clear_desc: Removes the WiFi network name and password from the companion. Reboot to apply the change.
cmd_wifi_status_desc: Shows whether the companion is connected to WiFi, and its IP address in your network. The companion takes connections from the app on that address, port 5000.
keygen_find_body: The Prefix tool shows which prefixes nodes already use, and suggests a free one.
keygen_needs_js: This tool runs in your browser and needs JavaScript.
keygen_prefix_hint: 2 characters for 1 byte, 4 for 2 bytes. The firmware refuses 00 and FF.
keygen_stopped: Stopped. Try again, or pick a shorter prefix.
keygen_bad: Type 2 or 4 hex characters (0-9, a-f), not starting with 00 or FF.
keygen_unsupported: Your browser cannot make Ed25519 keys. Use Chrome 137, Firefox 129, Safari 17 or newer.
keygen_set_body: Run this command on your repeater, then reboot it. It keeps its settings and access list, but becomes a new node for everyone. Add it again in the app after its first advert.
keygen_secret: This is your repeater's private key. Anyone who has it can act as your repeater, so keep it to yourself. Your browser made it, and this page sends it nowhere.
guides_card_keygen_desc: Give your repeater a prefix that no repeater near you uses.
ch_needs_js: The channel list runs in your browser and needs JavaScript. The Analyzer shows the same channels:
ch_error: The channel list did not load. Try again later; the key of any #name below still works.
ch_count: {n} channels heard in {country}, most messages first.
ch_calc_body: Type a channel name that starts with #. The key follows from the name, so you get the same key as the app.
guides_card_channels_desc: The channels people near you use, and how to join them.
area_other_presets_title: Other presets in the MeshCore app
area_other_presets_body: The app lists these European presets too, without naming an area for them. A 433 MHz preset needs a board with a 433 MHz radio.
net_live_packets: packets in the last full hour
net_live_countries: countries heard in the last hour
net_live_repeaters: repeaters heard in the last 7 days
net_join_body: Every observer shows a bit more of the mesh, for everyone in Europe. Pick the way that fits; the MeshCore Analyzer shows the steps.
net_way_app_desc: Pair a MeshCore radio with your phone over Bluetooth. The app reports what it hears, with nothing to flash.
net_way_browser_desc: Connect a radio over USB or Bluetooth in Chrome or Edge. The browser reports while the tab stays open.
net_way_board_desc: Flash observer firmware on a LoRa board. It reports by itself over Wi-Fi, day and night.
home_town_title: Follow one message across the rooftops.
home_town_lead: Your phone or laptop sends a message to your companion, over Bluetooth or USB. The companion sends it by radio to a repeater on the roof. From there it hops from roof to roof.
home_town_companion_desc: The radio you message from. Pair it with your phone or laptop, or pick one with its own screen and keyboard that works on its own.
home_town_repeater_desc: Passes messages on for everyone around it. Most run on solar power. You only need your own where the mesh does not reach yet.
home_town_repeater_link: When to put up a repeater
home_town_mesh_desc: Repeaters pass a message on as far as they hear each other. Regions keep it local.
planned.guides-filter.lead: Drop traffic your repeater should not pass on, with the packet filter.
planned.guides-filter.what.title: What the filter does
planned.guides-filter.what.desc: Which packets a repeater can drop, and how that keeps the mesh quiet.
planned.guides-filter.configs.title: Recommended configurations
planned.guides-filter.configs.desc: Ready-made settings for common cases, such as blocking a noisy channel.
planned.guides-filter.settings.title: Every setting
planned.guides-filter.settings.desc: Each filter setting with its command and what it changes.
planned.guides-mqtt.lead: Let your always-on board report what it hears to the MeshCore Analyzer.
planned.guides-mqtt.need.title: What you need
planned.guides-mqtt.need.desc: A board with observer firmware and Wi-Fi, and the address of a broker.
planned.guides-mqtt.settings.title: Settings
planned.guides-mqtt.settings.desc: The Wi-Fi, broker and topic settings your board needs.
planned.guides-mqtt.commands.title: Commands for your broker
planned.guides-mqtt.commands.desc: The commands to paste, filled in for the broker you pick.
planned.guides-mqtt.check.title: Check it works
planned.guides-mqtt.check.desc: How to find your observer on the MeshCore Analyzer.
net_data_lead: Every number on this site comes from people who listen and share what they hear.
net_data_from_body: Observers report what they hear over MQTT to a broker, a server that collects the reports. They report to mqtt.meshcore-analyzer.eu or to another broker the Analyzer reads. The KiekR app and the browser observer report too. The Analyzer also fetches CoreScope analysers whose owners agreed. Every broker and analyser is read with its owner's permission.
net_data_way_body: One message heard by many observers counts once. The Analyzer decodes it and builds the maps, the numbers and the channel list from it. It keeps each message, but what each observer heard stays 10 days. Hourly numbers stay up to 30 days, daily totals stay for good.
net_data_node_title: What others see of your node
net_data_node_body: Others see its name, its public key, its kind and its position if you share it. Your direct messages stay encrypted. Messages on Public and on hashtag channels are readable for anyone, the Analyzer included.
net_data_q1: Is my node on the map?
net_data_a1: Only when an observer heard its advert, the packet a node sends to announce itself. A node far from any observer stays off the map.
net_data_q2: Can the Analyzer read my direct messages?
net_data_a2: No. Only you and the other person hold the key.
net_data_q3: Can I send data from my own tool?
net_data_a3: Yes: publish over MQTT to mqtt.meshcore-analyzer.eu, signed with your node's key as an observer does. The {link} shows how to connect.
net_data_q4: Can I use the Analyzer's data?
net_data_a4: Ask on its {link} first. The Analyzer does not allow automated collection.
release.v1-18-0.1: Your companion gets a command line: open Command Line in the app, version 1.50 or later. A contact you give the Remote CLI permission can send it commands over the mesh.
release.v1-18-0.2: A newly set up repeater turns on minimal loop detection by itself.
release.v1-18-0.3: A repeater with its adverts off no longer shows up when others search for nodes.
release.v1-18-0.4: On ESP32 boards the clock survives a reboot, and most nRF52 boards no longer refuse to start on a low battery.
release.v1-18-0.5: New boards: Thinknode M4 and M8, Wio Tracker L1 1W, Muzi Base and Waveshare ESP32-S3 LR1121.
release.v1-18-0.6: The Bluetooth companion firmware also does WiFi on several boards, among them Heltec, Wireless Paper, RAK and Xiao S3; set it up in the app.
release.v1-17-1.1: On boards with an external amplifier, the receive gain setting is now saved. Check radio.fem.rxgain and radio.rxgain on your repeater after updating.
release.v1-17-1.2: Sending works again on the Heltec T096, and the T-Beam Supreme screen shows again.
release.v1-17-0.1: Every firmware stores its settings in a new format.
release.v1-17-0.2: A repeater switches off with a long press on its button. New commands: set cad for repeaters and room.post for room servers.
release.v1-17-0.3: nRF52 boards use their built-in encryption chip, and boards draw less power in hibernate and when switched off.
release.v1-17-0.4: New boards: Heltec V4 R8, RC32 and Tower V2, Thinknode M7 and M9, Sensecap MeshTracker X1, and radios with the LR2021 chip.
release.v1-17-0.5: Repeaters listen better before they send, so busy meshes have fewer collisions.
console_needs_js: The console needs JavaScript and a browser that can reach USB: Chrome, Edge or Opera on a computer.
console_status_idle: Plug in your node, then connect and pick its port.
console_status_asking: Connected. Asking your node what it is.
console_status_connected: Connected. Type a command and press Enter.
console_status_lost: The connection is gone. Check the cable and connect again.
console_status_busy: The port could not be opened. Close the other program or tab that uses it, then try again.
console_status_unsupported: This browser cannot reach USB. Use Chrome, Edge or Opera on a computer.
console_status_copy_failed: The log could not be copied. Select it and copy it by hand.
console_node_known: The suggestions show the commands this node understands.
console_node_unknown: Your node did not name its role. The suggestions show the commands of repeaters, room servers and sensors.
console_dmc_before: This node runs DutchMeshCore firmware. The suggestions show MeshCore's own commands. The DutchMeshCore commands are in the
console_trouble_1: Use a data cable. Some cables only charge.
console_trouble_2: Close other programs that use the port, such as another console or the flasher on this site in another tab.
console_trouble_3: Pick the right port: unplug your node, see which port disappears, and plug it in again.
console_trouble_4: Firefox and Safari cannot reach USB from a web page. Use Chrome, Edge or Opera on a computer.
usb_title: Send to your repeater over USB.
usb_body: Plug in your repeater, connect, and check what changes before you send.
usb_status_busy: The port is in use. Close the other program or tab that uses it, then try again.
usb_status_fill: Fill in {value} in the commands above first.
usb_status_review: Compare the current values with the new ones, then send.
usb_status_sent: Sent. Your repeater accepted every command.
usb_status_sent_errors: Sent, but your repeater refused some commands or did not answer. Check the replies.
usb_status_rebooted: The repeater restarts with its new radio settings.
flash_no_match: No board matches. Try a shorter word, or pick from the list.
flash_needs_js: The flasher needs JavaScript. Without it, {link} have every file.
flash_mode_update: Update: for a board that already runs MeshCore. Keeps your node's keys, contacts and settings.
flash_mode_fresh: Fresh install: for a new board or one with other firmware. Wipes the board, keys included.
flash_wipe_ok: I know a fresh install wipes my node's keys and contacts.
flash_esp_help: Chrome, Edge or Opera on a computer. If the board does not connect, hold its BOOT button (PRG on some boards) while you plug it in, then try again.
flash_uf2_title: Copy the file onto your board
flash_uf2_step2: Plug in your board and double-tap its reset button. It shows up as a USB drive. A board without a reset button has its own way in; its maker's page says how.
flash_uf2_step3: Drag the file onto that drive. The board restarts with the new firmware; an update keeps its keys.
flash_status_unsupported: This browser cannot reach USB. Use Chrome, Edge or Opera on a computer.
flash_status_no_list: The list of boards did not load. Reload the page.
flash_status_flashing: Flashing. Keep the board plugged in.
flash_status_done: Done. Your board restarts with the new firmware.
flash_status_failed: Flashing stopped. Hold the BOOT button while you plug the board in, then try again.
flash_status_no_file: The firmware file did not download. Try again in a moment.
flash_other_firmware: Other firmware, such as the DutchMeshCore observer firmware, comes with its own flasher: {link}.
